title: Filon Methods for Highly Oscillatory Controlled Quantum Systems
abstract: Fast and accurate classical simulation of quantum systems is a central challenge in the design and control of quantum computers, but the highly oscillatory dynamics of these systems severely limit the efficiency of standard numerical methods. To address this, we adapt Filon quadrature for oscillatory integrals into two numerical methods, called Filon and Controlled Filon, for solving linear systems of ODEs with highly oscillatory solutions. We tailor both methods for efficient implementation in controlled quantum systems, and the Controlled Filon method additionally accounts for the oscillatory structure of the control pulses. We show by numerical experiments that these methods significantly reduce the computational cost of accurately simulating systems of superconducting transmon qubits by decreasing the number of timesteps needed to reach a given level of precision, with only a modest increase in the cost per timestep. For a realistic simulation of the dynamics of a CNOT gate, the Controlled Filon method is the most efficient method tested at every target accuracy, outperforming the best Hermite method by up to 6x and the Hermite method of the same order by up to 500x.
summary: This paper introduces two novel numerical techniques, Filon and Controlled Filon methods, designed to efficiently simulate the time evolution of quantum systems with highly oscillatory behavior. By adapting Filon quadrature for oscillatory integrals, the authors drastically reduce the required number of simulation timesteps compared to established methods like Hermite integration. This makes accurate classical control simulations feasible for superconducting qubits.
main_problem: The core challenge is achieving fast and accurate classical simulation of quantum systems whose dynamics are governed by highly oscillatory time-dependent Hamiltonians.
main_result: The developed Controlled Filon method significantly reduces the computational cost compared to standard methods, outperforming benchmarks like the Hermite method by factors up to 500x for simulating gates like CNOT.
method: The authors adapt Filon quadrature, traditionally used for oscillatory integrals, into two specialized time-stepping schemes (Filon and Controlled Filon) tailored for solving linear systems of ODEs arising from quantum evolution.
model_or_system: The study focuses on controlled quantum systems modeled by the time-dependent Schrödinger equation ($ rac{d}{dt}\psi(t) = -iH(t)\psi(t)$), specifically tested using superconducting transmon qubits and CNOT gate simulations.
key_observables: Accuracy of simulation (convergence rate) for quantum state evolution, particularly when simulating controlled gates like the CNOT gate.
important_parameters: The time step size ($\Delta t$), the oscillation frequencies ($\omega_j$), and the order ($s$) of the interpolation polynomial used in the quadrature rule are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: A key assumption is that the envelope function $f(t)$ varies more slowly than the carrier wave $e^{i\omega t}$ when $|\omega| > 0$. The methods are derived assuming specific mathematical structures related to the Hamiltonian evolution.
figures_summary: Figure 2.1 compares convergence for the Rabi oscillator, showing that Filon/Controlled Filon achieve target accuracy with much larger time steps ($\Delta t$) than the Hermite method.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the problem (highly oscillatory quantum simulation), then details the adaptation of Filon quadrature theory into two numerical methods, followed by presenting and analyzing these methods through numerical simulations on physical systems like the Rabi oscillator and CNOT gate.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful algorithmic tool for simulating complex quantum dynamics where standard integrators fail due to rapid oscillations, directly impacting computational feasibility in quantum control theory.
